Serbia’s Assistant Minister of Finance was told how capital markets reform usually goes: you wait for the generation that lost money in the last crash to die.

“Our idea is that within five years, all of the IT systems of the Belgrade Stock Exchange, trading, core trading engine, all of the auxiliary systems, reporting, control, supervision, will be on blockchain.”

“Serbia, like many other countries, I would say majority, 120 to 140 countries around the world, faces a tough situation. It has a developed banking system. It has some alternatives in terms of access to finance, but really everything is with the banks. And it doesn’t have easy access to the global capital markets, and the global liquidity doesn’t have an easy access to us.”

“What the guys from Greece told us: you have to wait for the generation which lost money in the last crash to die. So for Serbia, our best bet is 2036 to start doing. So I’m not eager to wait another 10 years.”

Ognjen Popović, Assistant Minister at the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Serbia, at Solana Summit Serbia
